name: Weavr
subtitle: Weavr for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV
description: Unsigned Weavr builds for iOS and tvOS. Add this source to Feather (or any AltStore-compatible signer) to install and update Weavr.

apps.name: Weavr iOS
apps.subtitle: 26 Nov 11:45 GMT · Multi-source IPTV with automatic failover
apps.localizedDescription: Weavr merges your M3U and Xtream sources into one library, removes duplicate channels and films across providers, and fails over to another source when a stream stalls. Includes a TV guide, films and series, continue watching, Picture in Picture, AirPlay, and WeavrLink, a remote for your Weavr TVs.

versions.localizedDescription:
Sport tiles near-square, as every tile in the app

The game cards' corners as the posters' (16 to the tiles' 3), and their
LIVE and channel badges shaped as a poster's badges.

Silo collections: every group back; only a true double (same id and name) kept once

Kept once on its id alone, the libraries' collections could all be taken
for your own when Silo's list of yours carries them too: filed under one
library's name (Movies) and asked for as yours. Now only one listed in
both with the same id and name is kept once — the library's, read as a
library's (one of your own then asked for as yours), in the group your
list files it in where that's one of Silo's. Shelf folders pointed at your
own copy are pointed back at the collection as Silo lists it. The log
says each group and how many.
ThreadPlayer: the opened line's name no longer clashes with the demuxer it opened

Log: the app not responding noted as it happens; pages noted on the TV

- A watchdog on the main thread (both apps): stuck 4 s or more is noted
  with the memory in use, again every 10 s while it lasts; responding
  again after 8 s or more is a "Stopped responding for N s" line with
  what it was doing. Paused while the app's in the background
- A run that ended stuck says so at the next start ("stopped responding
  and was ended"), with what was on screen before it; the end message
  says tvOS on the TV, not iOS
- Noted as they open: the TV's menu pages, and Settings > Sport's pages,
  so a stall there shows where it was

ThreadPlayer, Weavr's own player (Settings > Playback > Player): every format, Dolby Vision 5, 7 and 8, DTS and TrueHD to 7.1, styled ASS subtitles, AV1, Picture in Picture, AirPlay. Also: episode descriptions open out, iPhone plays in landscape with a rotate button, gentler on providers, Copy from your Weavr TV fixed.
Grid build fixes: argument order, the circuit's own point type, board map

Sources on three lines; the Duo's Search, Settings and WeavrLink full screen

- Every source list (iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, the player's): the source,
  then its pills (quality, picture, sound), then what makes it another
  version (an edition, Silo's part and file) or a channel's provider and
  group. The pills wrap where there are many; the iOS sheet sized to fit.
- The Duo: Search, Settings and WeavrLink take the whole screen rather
  than a sheet floating short of its edges with the strip cutting into
  it. Search and Settings draw their own top row (name, Done, the search
  field the width of the page), as the Duo's pages do; WeavrLink's TV
  settings button sits by the switcher, out of the strip.
- The chip layout moved to the shared code, for both apps.

Silo plays as the TV app does

- Asked as the TV app asks: its features (playback_plan_v3 only) and its
  list of what it plays, word for word (the original, a progressive copy
  or HLS; MKV, DTS, TrueHD and the rest); only the device named as it is.
- One player for it all, as the TV app: VLC, through the relay that adds
  the sign-in. Apple's player only for Dolby Vision (Settings) or where
  Apple's player alone is chosen; no sniffing first.
- A title's best version in Silo's own order within a resolution.
- The keep-alive every 15 seconds, as the TV app.
- A session that started but won't play: Silo asked why while it's still
  open, logged, then closed. The log says who played it, how long Silo
  took and how it's sent.

Blur unwatched episodes, for every show or one show at a time

- Settings > Playback > Films & series: Blur unwatched episodes. Pictures
  of episodes not watched (nor started) are blurred on a show's page, so
  they give nothing away; watched and started ones show as they are.
- Each show can choose for itself: the "..." by its season (iPhone, iPad)
  or Hide spoilers / Spoilers hidden by its buttons (Apple TV). A show's
  choice that matches the setting for every show is no choice of its own:
  it follows that setting from then on. Kept per profile.

A film's cuts are one film, each cut shown on its copies

As Silo's own apps and the TV app do it: Gladiator is one film, and its
Director's Cut is picked in its source list, with its own qualities.
- Silo's versions show their edition ("Extended", "Director's Cut") and
  any part ("Part 1 of 2") on their row's second line.
- Xtream films: a cut named in the panel's title ("Gladiator (Director's
  Cut)", "Aliens Special Edition", "Apocalypse Now: Redux") is taken off the
  film's title, so it's one film with the plain release, and kept on its
  copy's second line instead. Only where it's plainly a cut (in brackets,
  after a dash or colon, or a cut's full name at the end): "Uncut Gems"
  stays as it is. In effect from each panel's next read.
- The source list never folds two cuts into one row, whatever their
  quality.

Shows open on season 1, not the specials

A show with a season 0 (specials) opened on it, and Play started its first
special: what's up next was the first unwatched episode in order, and the
specials come first. Up next now goes by the show's own seasons, with the
specials only when it has nothing else; the page opens on that season (else
the first numbered one), and season 0 stays in the list to go back to.

Apple TV: no gap in the sport row, no getting stuck in a game, nothing playing on after Back

- Home's sport row (and the Sport page's events): each game once. A game
  in two of the leagues followed came twice, and two cards with one id
  left a card-wide gap in the row.
- A channel picked for a game plays once its list has closed: shown while
  the list was still closing, the player didn't appear on the Apple TV,
  the game played on unseen and nothing else would open.
- The player's page closed some other way than its own Close or Back (the
  Apple TV's Menu pressed with a button focused, which the system takes)
  stops what's playing, rather than leaving it playing behind the menus;
  not when it's gone to the little window.

Silo's big reads complete instead of failing for good; a short read keeps what it brought

Silo's series read kept "not coming back whole", so its stored list was
never replaced: 95,989 shows stored against Silo's 84,904 now, the extra
being shows Silo has since removed or moved to new ids (VisionQuest's
series-tvdb-426606 answering 404).
- A stretch of the list that hasn't met the next stretch's first title
  where expected (Silo's list changes as it's read, and its seek needn't
  land exactly) reads on, up to three times its length, rather than
  failing the whole read after two extra pages.
- A read that still doesn't come back whole keeps what it brought that
  isn't stored (new titles, moved ids) and takes nothing away; the
  library's made again for them. It was all thrown away.
- The count shown while reading is what's kept, every stretch's first page
  included: a whole read now reaches Silo's total rather than ending
  about 2,000 short.

Fetch missing and Merge again, from a source's page

- A media server's films and series: how many it says it has, kept as
  it's read, beside how many are stored ("Silo has 12,400: 600 missing").
- Fetch missing: the server read again with every title it gives kept and
  added to what's stored (none taken away, one already there passed over),
  so a big read that stops part way still brings in what it got; the
  library is made again if anything came. No "couldn't reach" or resting
  for a top-up.
- Merge again, when most of what a source has stored isn't in the library:
  the library made from what's stored, nothing asked of the sources.

A source's films and series as stored, on its own page

Settings > Sources > a source (on Apple TV, the source's menu > What's
stored): its films and series as its last complete read gave them, when
that was, and how many titles in the library carry it, so what's meant to
be there and what is can be seen side by side. A kind never read whole,
or read but with nothing from it in the library, shows in red.

apps.name: Weavr tvOS
apps.subtitle: 26 Nov 13:07 GMT · Weavr on Apple TV
apps.localizedDescription: Weavr for Apple TV: your merged IPTV library, TV guide, films and series with automatic failover between sources.

versions.localizedDescription:
WeavrLink: the Apple TV's shelves and folders from the phone, photos included

- The Apple TV answers the phone's shelf editor at last (it sent no
  shelves and turned every change down): shelves added, renamed, moved,
  hidden, shaped; folders added, renamed, moved, featured, hidden; an
  AIOMetadata install's catalogues imported
- Add a folder on the phone offers what the TV has: its Silo collections
  and libraries and its provider's categories (asked of the TV), and the
  streaming services and genres, ticked and added in one go
- A folder's picture from the phone: an address, or a photo from the
  phone's library, made no bigger than it's shown and sent to the TV,
  which keeps it; its own, never replaced by the source's
- Swipe a folder to lock it with the TV's category PIN, or unlock it
